subject: Moraine dedicated sizing: throughput targets, SLO fit & slab recommendation
messages:
From: Lucas Ford <lucas.ford@moraine.ai>

Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@moraine.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Moraine inference needs — rough throughput & latency targets

Kimberly / Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. To get internal alignment for procurement we need a short TCO + sizing note that ties our expected traffic to an SLO target. High level context: we are launching a summarization feature (customers submit documents, model returns ~300-700 tokens). Expected ramp: 50k active users in month 1, average 0.6 requests/user/day, spike factor 4 at peak hour.

Two asks:
- Please give tokens/sec estimates and a recommended reserved slab (GPU type and count) that meets p95 latency <= 600ms for the live model.
- Call out headroom assumptions and fallback mode if we exceed reserved capacity.

Can you send a single-slide style recommendation + any spreadsheet backing? Procurement would like to see numbers before Friday.

— Lucas
Director, Platform 
Moraine AI
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Lucas Ford <lucas.ford@moraine.ai>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@moraine.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Moraine inference needs — rough throughput & latency targets

Lucas / Sana — attaching a modeling workbook and a short SLO matrix (see attachments). Summary below; full assumptions and per-model microbench are in the spreadsheet.

Quick recommendation (executive summary):
- Target sustained throughput: 18,500 tokens/sec (this maps to 50k users * 0.6 req/day with 4x peak hour & avg response 450 tokens).
- P95 latency target: <= 600ms (redwood measurement, network excluded).
- Recommended reserved slab: 12 x A100-80GB (baseline) with 25% capacity headroom => propose committing 15 x A100-80GB. This gives an effective burst cushion while keeping sustained p95 under 600ms for our tested model variant.

Modeling notes / reasoning:
- Model: curated open LLM (prod variant ~70B, quantized to INT8). Measured on our runtime with KV caching enabled: median token throughput per A100-80GB: ~1,600 tokens/sec for streaming generation at batch size 8; p95 token latency mapping yields ~500-550ms at that throughput.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU for typical request mix ~= 1,230 tps (because of 450-token median responses and KV reset frequency). 12 GPUs * 1,230 = 14,760 tps base; to hit 18,500 tps we rely on autoscaling burst capacity + batching improvements during peak (effective multiplier ~1.25). We therefore recommend committing 15 GPUs to ensure the service stays within p95 SLO during sustained peak.
- Headroom and safety: 25% reserved headroom (15 vs baseline 12) to cover unmodeled tail-loads, KV cache churn during large document sizes, and spikes from new customer cohorts.

Fallback plan if demand exceeds reserved slab:
- Automatic routing to hosted fallback variant (smaller model 13B INT4) for degraded latency-sensitive requests (configured as route policy).
- Degraded responses limited to non-critical customers for 30–45 minutes while ops brings additional burst capacity.

Deliverables attached: moraine_tokens_modeling.xlsx (per-minute sims), moraine_slo_matrix.pdf (SLO mapping & canary plan), draft_sow_moraine.docx (SOW stub including commitment/overage terms).

I can join a quick procurement call Thursday afternoon if helpful.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Lucas — quick follow-up from commercial side.

Thanks Kim — spreadsheet looks good. A couple of clarifications procurement will ask for:
- Commit sizing: we proposed 15 x A100-80GB. Can we offer a stepped commitment (12 committed + 3 optional reserved month-to-month) to reduce upfront dollar commitment?
- Overage pricing: if they go into burst beyond the 15 GPUs, can we set burst pads at a fixed per-token premium with an automatic notification threshold at 85% slab utilization?

Marcus — can you confirm whether the INT8 variant we profiled has the same memory footprint for 80GB SKUs or if we should flip to 2x smaller GPUs for better packing? Lucas, cc'ing Marcus for that detail.

—Priyom
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Lucas Ford <lucas.ford@moraine.ai>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@moraine.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T16:44:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Moraine inference needs — rough throughput & latency targets

Priyom / team / Lucas — quick engineering confirmation.

Confirmed details from runtime testing (notes pulled into spreadsheet):
- INT8 variant used for the modeling fits comfortably on A100-80GB with room for KV cache for ~12 concurrent long-context (up to 8k tokens) sessions per GPU. Memory headroom observed ~18% in our tests (with sharded KV).
- If Moraine prefers smaller hardware for lower list price, 2 x A40-48GB configs increase packing inefficiency and will raise p95 by ~12–15% at equivalent token throughput due to reduced per-GPU kernel parallelism. My recommendation stands: commit to 12 A100s baseline but price/contract to 15 for 25% buffer.
- Operational runbook: enable prefix caching for frequent documents (expected cache hit 42% by our simulated corpus) which increases effective tokens/sec per GPU by ~18% during normal traffic and reduces cold-start tail. We'll enable a canary (5% traffic) with rollback on p95 drift > 50ms.

Next steps: Priyom / Kim, if procurement agrees to stepped commitment, I can author the SLO appendix that defines the 85% utilization alert, burst premium rate, and the automated fallback routing.

—Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
